year, month, and day fix the calendar date, carrier and flight identify the scheduled service, and origin disambiguates carriers that reuse flight numbers from different NYC airports; all six columns have null_rate 0.0 in bronze and are proposed required.

dep_time (null_rate 0.029388), arr_time (0.0307), dep_delay and arr_delay and air_time (0.032981) are null together for flights that never departed, per operator context, so nulls are retained rather than imputed or dropped.

year, month, day, dep_time, sched_dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, sched_arr_time, arr_delay, flight, air_time, distance, hour, and minute land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample is integral (e.g. month samples 1.0-6.0, hour samples 5.0-23.0), so they are cast to INTEGER.

purpose: This table holds cleaned NYC flight departure records for January-June 2013 from JFK, LGA, and EWR, feeding downstream analytics on carrier punctuality, route volume, and delay patterns.
usage: Join on the declared grain of year, month, day, carrier, flight, and origin; treat dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay, arr_delay, and air_time as nullable and filter or branch logic deliberately when they are null, since those nulls mark flights that never departed rather than missing measurements.
limitations: Roughly 3% of rows lack actual departure and arrival times, delays, and air time because the flight never departed, and about 0.9% of rows lack a tail number; these nulls were retained rather than resolved, and no duplicate rows were found to exclude since duplicate_row_rate is 0.0.
